boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Marist settings for studying, meeting, making, viewing art, recreation, and campus events; check each location’s current access rules before going.

cards.title: James A. Cannavino Library
cards.subtitle: Library study areas, computer lab, and atrium gathering space
cards.notes: Choose seating that fits your task, then use the library’s desktops or laptop loans. The top floor also houses academic-support services.
cards.short_summary: A three-floor library built for both individual and group work.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist states that Cannavino Library offers seating for individual and group studying, is the campus’s largest computer lab, and has academic-support functions on its top floor.
cards.source_title: James A. Cannavino Library | Marist University
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to current library policies and building access.

cards.title: Murray Student Center
cards.subtitle: Campus hub for meetings, services, lounges, and events
cards.notes: Use the lounges or meeting areas as a starting point for a club gathering, then check the building’s current facility hours before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A student-services and activities hub with lounges, meeting rooms, dining, theatre, and music spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist describes the Murray Student Center as a focal point for university life where students meet, organize, and attend events; it lists lounges and meeting rooms among its facilities.
cards.access_notes: Facility hours and room availability vary; follow current Student Center policies.

cards.title: Fern Tor
cards.subtitle: 13-acre nature preserve at the north end of campus
cards.notes: Take the marked trail network for a daylight reset or nature observation. Stay on established paths and plan around the sunrise-to-sundown schedule.
cards.short_summary: A campus nature preserve with trails, a pond, creek, and Hudson River overlook.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist identifies Fern Tor as a 13-acre campus nature preserve with an accessible trail network, a creek and pond, and hours from sunrise to sundown.
cards.access_notes: Open sunrise to sundown; use established trails and observe preserve guidance.

cards.title: Longview Park
cards.subtitle: Marist riverfront park on the Hudson River
cards.notes: Bring coursework or meet friends by the waterfront during daylight, and look for Student Activities programming when an event is scheduled there.
cards.short_summary: A 12-acre riverfront setting with direct waterfront access for the Marist community.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist’s self-guided tour says Longview Park is open to the Marist community, provides students direct waterfront access, and hosts Student Activities and Student Programming Council events.
cards.access_notes: Waterfront conditions and event access vary; follow posted site guidance.

cards.title: Maker Lab
cards.subtitle: Steel Plant creative workspace for Red Foxes
cards.notes: Check the workshop schedule, then bring a class project or creative idea. Ask about materials before assuming a personal project has no supply cost.
cards.short_summary: A Steel Plant making space with equipment, workshops, and project materials.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist reports that the Maker Lab in Steel Plant is open to all Red Foxes and that students use its equipment and resources for creative work.
cards.source_title: Maker Lab Sparks Creativity and Community | Marist University
cards.access_notes: Availability, supervision, and material costs can vary by project and workshop.

cards.title: Marist Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Exhibition gallery in Steel Plant Studios
cards.notes: Check the gallery calendar before visiting, then spend time with the current exhibition or attend an announced student, faculty, or community reception.
cards.short_summary: A Steel Plant gallery that presents exhibitions, including student-led work.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist documented a student-led exhibition at the Marist Art Gallery in Steel Plant Studios attended by students, faculty, staff, and community members.
cards.source_title: Student Captures Asia Study Abroad Experience Through Art | Marist University
cards.access_notes: Exhibitions and public hours change; confirm the current show and access details.

cards.title: James J. McCann Recreational Center
cards.subtitle: Recreation center with fitness, intramural, and aquatic facilities
cards.notes: Use the campus map to locate the fitness, club and intramural, arena, and natatorium facilities, then confirm eligibility and operating details with Recreation.
cards.short_summary: Marist’s central recreation complex for fitness, aquatics, intramurals, and athletics.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist’s campus map lists the James J. McCann Recreational Center with a fitness center, club and intramural center, natatorium, arena, and aerobic center.
cards.access_notes: Facility access and program participation are subject to current Recreation policies.

cards.title: Lowell Thomas Communications Center
cards.subtitle: Communication and arts building with Media Center and community offices
cards.notes: Use the campus map to find the Media Center and School of Communication and the Arts, and check department guidance before seeking access to specialized spaces.
cards.short_summary: A named academic setting for communication, media, and arts-related work.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist’s campus map lists the Lowell Thomas Communications Center as home to the School of Communication and the Arts, Media Center, and Center for Social Media.
cards.access_notes: Specialized labs and media spaces may have departmental access requirements.

cards.title: Dyson Center
cards.subtitle: Academic building with Idea Lab, mock courtroom, and student-run café
cards.notes: Meet classmates around your schedule, then use the building’s named learning spaces when they are available. Respect any class, lab, or event reservations.
cards.short_summary: A multidisciplinary academic building with several named applied-learning spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist’s campus map lists Dyson Center with the Idea Lab, Investment Center, Marketing Lab, Mock Courtroom, and Saxbys student-run café.
cards.access_notes: Classroom, lab, and café access depend on current schedules and policies.

cards.title: Cornell Boathouse
cards.subtitle: Historic riverfront boathouse in Longview Park
cards.notes: Notice the restored historic structure from Longview Park, and attend only university or community functions for which you are invited or registered.
cards.short_summary: A restored historic boathouse whose upper floor hosts campus meetings and events.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist says the Cornell Boathouse’s second level hosts campus luncheons, meetings, and other events, while the building remains a functional boathouse.
cards.access_notes: Not a drop-in venue; enter only for authorized functions or permitted access.
